s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive pigmented lip lesion with local extension and ulceration
salient_findings: Slowly enlarging pigmented lesion on the upper left lip vermilion
Brownish discoloration of the skin above the vermilion
Multiple pigmented papules with focal ulcerations on the lip
key_facts: 4-year history of the lesion
Initial lesion size: 1 cm × 0.5 cm
Lesion progressively increased in size without symptoms
Brownish discoloration of the skin above the vermilion appeared after 3 years
Multiple pigmented papules of various sizes on the vermilion
Lip slightly swollen
Intraoral lesion: 1.5 cm, non-tender, non-indurated, with focal ulcerations
No cervical lymphadenopathy or other skin lesions
Normal complete blood count, biochemical profile, and urinalysis
Unremarkable chest radiography

shortlist.label: Malignant Melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive pigmented lip lesion with ulceration

shortlist.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Ulcerated lesion on the lip with local extension

shortlist.label: Pigmented Basal Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Pigmented lesion on the lip with gradual enlargement

shortlist.label: Desmoplastic Melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive pigmented lesion with local invasion

shortlist.label: Mucosal Melanosis
shortlist.why_kept: Pigmented lesion on the lip and intraoral mucosa

raw.rationale: The patient's 4-year history of a progressively enlarging pigmented lesion on the lip, with brownish discoloration and multiple pigmented papules, is highly suggestive of malignant melanoma, particularly given the presence of an intraoral lesion with focal ulcerations.

rejected.label: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the description of the lesion as a pigmented macule with brownish discoloration and multiple pigmented papules is less typical for squamous cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Pigmented Basal Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: Pigmented basal cell carcinoma is less likely given the location on the lip and the presence of an intraoral lesion with focal ulcerations.

rejected.label: Desmoplastic Melanoma
rejected.why: Desmoplastic melanoma is a rare variant of melanoma, and while it can present with a pigmented lesion, the description provided does not specifically suggest desmoplastic features.

rejected.label: Mucosal Melanosis
rejected.why: Mucosal melanosis typically presents with diffuse pigmentation rather than a discrete, enlarging lesion, making it less likely in this case.
